linkTypes.direct: Explicit parent-child or biological descent within primary canonical/ancient texts
linkTypes.expansion: Matriarchs, additional children, royal successions, or migrations supplied by extra-biblical or secondary chronicles (Book of Jasher, Jubilees, 1 Enoch, Sumerian King List, Bundahishn, Shahnameh, Shiji, Puranas)
linkTypes.cognate: Linguistically or historically attested cross-tradition identity/ethnonym bridge (e.g., Vedic Vivasvan/Yama/Aptya = Avestan Vivanghant/Yima/Athwya; Biblical Madai = Medes; Mizraim = Phoenician Misor/Egypt)
linkTypes.parallel: Independent structural/archetypal parallel across ancient corpora (Great Flood survivors, 7th antediluvian sage, Adapa/Adam, Sargon/Moses basket, tripartite world division)
linkTypes.syncretic: Ancient, Greco-Egyptian, or medieval chronicler identification bridging figures across cultures (e.g., Enoch = Thoth/Saurid; Moses = Osarseph/Musaeus; Japheth = Oghuz Khagan; Zepho = King of Kittim/Rome)

nodes.name: Primordial Human Ancestors
nodes.notes: Structural hub linking the first humans fashioned from clay, earth, or cosmic life across Near Eastern, Indo-Iranian, and East Asian texts.

nodes.name: Great Flood / Cataclysm Survivors
nodes.notes: Global ancestral bottleneck motif where a righteous survivor preserves humanity and restarts post-cataclysm lineages.

nodes.name: Post-Flood Division of Nations
nodes.notes: Genealogical maps dividing humanity across Eurasia and Africa through sons of a universal ancestor.

nodes.name: Adam & Eve (Hawwah)
nodes.notes: First human couple. Book of Jasher 1:12-13 notes they bore two sons (Cain, Abel) and three daughters; Jubilees 4 explicitly names their daughters Awan and Azura.

nodes.name: Abel (Hevel)
nodes.notes: Shepherd slain by Cain. In Jasher 1:13-25 the conflict involves the division of fields, flocks, and twin sisters.

nodes.name: Cain (Qayin) & Awan
nodes.role: Firstborn / Builder of City of Enoch
nodes.notes: Founder of the Cainite line. Jubilees 4:9 names his wife Awan (his sister). Jasher 2:26-27 recounts his accidental death by blind Lamech's arrow.

nodes.name: Seth (Shet) & Azura
nodes.notes: Appointed in place of Abel. Jubilees 4:11 names his wife Azura. Josephus credits Seth's descendants with inventing astronomy and inscribing it on two pillars to survive flood and fire.

nodes.name: Enoch (son of Cain)
nodes.notes: Eponym of the first city built by Cain.

nodes.name: Irad
nodes.notes: Son of Cainite Enoch.

nodes.name: Mehujael
nodes.notes: Son of Irad.

nodes.name: Methushael
nodes.notes: Son of Mehujael; father of Cainite Lamech.

nodes.name: Lamech (Cainite)
nodes.notes: Marries Adah and Zillah (daughters of Sethite Cainan in Jasher 2:18!). Father of Jabal, Jubal, Tubal-cain, and Naamah.

nodes.name: Jabal
nodes.notes: Son of Lamech & Adah; father of those who dwell in tents and keep livestock.

nodes.name: Jubal
nodes.notes: Son of Lamech & Adah; inventor of harp and flute/organ.

nodes.name: Tubal-cain
nodes.notes: Son of Lamech & Zillah. Jasher 2:26-27 relates how he guided blind Lamech's bow, accidentally killing Cain before being slain by Lamech.

nodes.name: Naamah (dau. of Lamech)
nodes.notes: Named in Genesis 4:22. Rabbinic tradition (Genesis Rabbah 23:3) identifies her as Noah's wife (while Book of Jasher 5:15 names Noah's wife as Naamah daughter of Enoch).

nodes.name: Enosh & Noam
nodes.notes: Jubilees 4:13 names his wife Noam. Jasher 2:4-7 says idol worship began in his days and the sea (Gihon) flooded a third of the earth.

nodes.name: Kenan (Cainan) & Mualeleth
nodes.notes: Jubilees 4:14 names his wife Mualeleth. Book of Jasher 2:11-12 says Kenan ruled wisely, inscribed prophecies of the Flood on stone tablets, and fathered 3 sons (Mahalalel, Enan, Mered) and 2 daughters (Adah, Zillah).

nodes.name: Mahalalel & Dinah
nodes.notes: Jubilees 4:15 names his wife Dinah, daughter of Barakiel.

nodes.name: Jared (Yered) & Baraka
nodes.notes: Jubilees 4:16 names his wife Baraka (dau. of Rasujal). 1 Enoch 6 and Jubilees 4:15 connect his name ('descent') to the descent of the Watchers on Mount Hermon.

nodes.name: Enoch (Khanokh) & Edni
nodes.notes: 7th from Adam; lived 365 years and ascended to heaven. Jubilees 4:17 credits him as first to learn writing, calendar, and astronomy. Book of Jasher 3:1 names his 3 sons (Methuselah, Elisha, Elimelech) and 2 daughters (Melca, Nahmah/Naamah). Widely equated in Greco-Egyptian & Arabic lore with Thoth/Hermes/King Saurid and compared to 7th Sumerian king Enmeduranki!

nodes.name: Methuselah & Edna
nodes.notes: Custodian of Enoch's books. Jubilees 4:27 names his wife Edna. Jasher 5:35 also names his son Eliakim, whose 3 daughters marry Noah's 3 sons!

nodes.name: Lamech (Sethite) & Betenos / Ashmua
nodes.notes: Jubilees 4:28 names his wife Betenos; Book of Jasher 4:11 names her Ashmua, daughter of Elisha son of Enoch! 1 Enoch 106 & Qumran 1Q20 recount his awe at Noah's luminous birth.

nodes.name: Noah (Noach) & Emzara / Naamah
nodes.notes: Called Noah by Lamech and Menahem by Methuselah (Jasher 4:14). Jubilees 4:33 names his wife Emzara; Jasher 5:15 names her Naamah daughter of Enoch (while Genesis Rabbah identifies her with Cainite Naamah). Father of Japheth, Ham, and Shem.

nodes.name: Enan (son of Kenan)
nodes.notes: Listed in Book of Jasher 2:11 as one of Kenan's three sons alongside Mahalalel and Mered.

nodes.name: Mered (son of Kenan)
nodes.notes: Listed in Book of Jasher 2:11 as one of Kenan's three sons.

nodes.name: Adah (dau. of Kenan)
nodes.notes: In Book of Jasher 2:18, Adah daughter of Sethite Kenan marries Cainite Lamech (mother of Jabal & Jubal), bridging the Sethite and Cainite lines!

nodes.name: Zillah (dau. of Kenan)
nodes.notes: In Book of Jasher 2:18, Zillah daughter of Sethite Kenan marries Cainite Lamech (mother of Tubal-cain & Naamah).

nodes.name: Elisha (son of Enoch)
nodes.notes: Son of Enoch in Jasher 3:1; father of Ashmua, who marries Lamech and births Noah (Jasher 4:11)!

nodes.name: Elimelech (son of Enoch)
nodes.notes: One of three sons of Enoch named in Book of Jasher 3:1.

nodes.name: Melca (dau. of Enoch)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Enoch named in Book of Jasher 3:1.

nodes.name: Naamah (dau. of Enoch)
nodes.notes: Named in Book of Jasher 3:1 & 5:15 as daughter of Enoch who marries Noah (at age 580) and becomes mother of Shem, Ham, and Japheth!

nodes.name: Eliakim (son of Methuselah)
nodes.notes: Named in Book of Jasher 5:35 as son of Methuselah whose three daughters Noah chose as wives for Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

nodes.name: The Watchers (Semyaza & Azazel)
nodes.notes: 200 Watchers descend on Mount Hermon in the days of Jared; chiefs include Semyaza, Azazel (metallurgy/weapons), Araqiel, Kokabiel, Baraqiel, Armaros, Penemue, and Gadreel.

nodes.name: Ohya & Hahya (Nephilim Giants)
nodes.notes: Named Giant brothers in the Dead Sea Scrolls Book of Giants who dream of the impending Flood and send Mahaway to ask Enoch to interpret it.

nodes.name: Mahaway (Giant Messenger)
nodes.notes: Winged Giant son of Baraqiel who flies across the world to consult Enoch on behalf of the Nephilim.

nodes.name: Ham (Cham) & Na'eltama'uk
nodes.role: Progenitor of Cush, Mizraim, Phut, Canaan
nodes.notes: Assigned Africa and southern lands in Jubilees 8. Father of Cush, Mizraim (Egypt), Phut (Libya/Punt), and Canaan.

nodes.name: Shem (Sem) & Sedeqetelebab
nodes.role: Progenitor of Semitic & Near Eastern Nations
nodes.notes: Assigned central Asia from the Mediterranean to India (Tinas) in Jubilees 8. Father of Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram.

nodes.name: Japheth (Yefet) & Adataneses
nodes.notes: Assigned Europe, Anatolia, Iranian highlands, and Northern Eurasia in Jubilees 8. Father of Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.

nodes.name: Gomer
nodes.notes: Father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah. Jasher 10:8 locates his descendants along the Franca/European rivers.

nodes.name: Magog
nodes.notes: Josephus identifies Magog with the Scythians; Jasher 7:4 names his sons Elichanaf and Lubal.

nodes.name: Madai (Medes)
nodes.notes: Direct historical cognate of the Medes. Jubilees 10:35 says Madai married a daughter of Shem and settled the Iranian plateau. Jasher 7:5 lists his 4 sons: Achon, Zeelo, Chazoni, Lot.

nodes.name: Javan (Ionians / Greeks)
nodes.notes: Linguistic cognate of Ionia. Father of Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.

nodes.name: Tubal
nodes.notes: Jasher 7:7 names his 3 sons: Ariphi, Kesed, Taari (Jasher 10:12 places Tubal in Tuscany/Pisa).

nodes.name: Meshech
nodes.notes: Jasher 7:8 names his 3 sons: Dedon, Zaron, Shebashni.

nodes.name: Tiras
nodes.notes: Jasher 7:9 names his 4 sons: Benib, Gera, Lupirion, Gilak (Jasher 10:14 links Tiras to Rushash/Kushni/Ongolis).

nodes.name: Ashkenaz
nodes.notes: Assyrian Ashkuza (Scythians); later medieval Jewish name for Rhineland/Germany.

nodes.name: Riphath (Rephath)
nodes.notes: Associated by Josephus with Paphlagonia; Jasher 10:9 connects Rephath with Western Europe (Bartonim/Bretons).

nodes.name: Togarmah
nodes.notes: Armenian chronicles (Moses of Chorene) trace Armenians to Togarmah; Book of Jasher 10:10 (via Josippon) lists 10 sons representing Turkic, Bulgar, Khazar, Pecheneg, and Hungarian steppe tribes!

nodes.name: Buzar (Cozar / Khazars)
nodes.notes: Son of Togarmah in Book of Jasher 10:10; linked to the Khazars.

nodes.name: Parzunac (Pechenegs)
nodes.notes: Son of Togarmah in Book of Jasher 10:10.

nodes.name: Balgar (Bulgars)
nodes.notes: Son of Togarmah in Book of Jasher 10:10; linked to the Volga/Danube Bulgars.

nodes.name: Elicanum
nodes.notes: Son of Togarmah in Book of Jasher 10:10.

nodes.name: Ragbib
nodes.notes: Son of Togarmah in Book of Jasher 10:10.

nodes.name: Tarki (Turks)
nodes.notes: Son of Togarmah in Book of Jasher 10:10 — explicit Jasher/Josippon bridge from Japheth to the Turkic peoples of the Eurasian Steppe!

nodes.name: Bid
nodes.notes: Son of Togarmah in Book of Jasher 10:10.

nodes.name: Zebuc
nodes.notes: Son of Togarmah in Book of Jasher 10:10.

nodes.name: Ongal (Onogurs / Hungarians)
nodes.notes: Son of Togarmah in Book of Jasher 10:10.

nodes.name: Tilmaz
nodes.notes: Son of Togarmah in Book of Jasher 10:10.

nodes.name: Elichanaf
nodes.notes: Son of Magog listed in Book of Jasher 7:4.

nodes.name: Lubal
nodes.notes: Son of Magog listed in Book of Jasher 7:4.

nodes.name: Achon
nodes.notes: Son of Madai listed in Book of Jasher 7:5.

nodes.name: Zeelo
nodes.notes: Son of Madai listed in Book of Jasher 7:5.

nodes.name: Chazoni
nodes.notes: Son of Madai listed in Book of Jasher 7:5.

nodes.name: Lot (son of Madai)
nodes.notes: Son of Madai listed in Book of Jasher 7:5.

nodes.name: Elishah
nodes.notes: Historically Alashiya (Cyprus); Jasher 10:15 links his descendants to the Almanim/Lombards.

nodes.name: Tarshish
nodes.notes: Mediterranean maritime center (Tartessos in Spain or Tarsus in Cilicia).

nodes.name: Kittim (Chittim)
nodes.notes: Historically Kition (Cyprus) and western Mediterranean islands. In Book of Jasher 10:16 & 61, Kittim settles Italy/Rome (Romim), where Esau's grandson Zepho becomes king!

nodes.name: Dodanim (Rodanim)
nodes.notes: Historically Rhodes (Rodanim in 1 Chr 1:7/LXX); Jasher 10:17 links them to Mediterranean coastal peoples.

nodes.name: Ariphi
nodes.notes: Son of Tubal in Book of Jasher 7:7.

nodes.name: Kesed
nodes.notes: Son of Tubal in Book of Jasher 7:7.

nodes.name: Taari
nodes.notes: Son of Tubal in Book of Jasher 7:7.

nodes.name: Dedon
nodes.notes: Son of Meshech in Book of Jasher 7:8.

nodes.name: Zaron
nodes.notes: Son of Meshech in Book of Jasher 7:8.

nodes.name: Shebashni
nodes.notes: Son of Meshech in Book of Jasher 7:8.

nodes.name: Benib
nodes.notes: Son of Tiras in Book of Jasher 7:9.

nodes.name: Gera
nodes.notes: Son of Tiras in Book of Jasher 7:9.

nodes.name: Lupirion
nodes.notes: Son of Tiras in Book of Jasher 7:9.

nodes.name: Gilak
nodes.notes: Son of Tiras in Book of Jasher 7:9.

nodes.name: Cush (Kush)
nodes.role: Eponym of Nubia/Ethiopia & Father of Nimrod
nodes.notes: Progenitor of Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, Sabteca, and Nimrod. Jasher 7:24 says Cush inherited Adam's garments from Ham and gave them to Nimrod.

nodes.name: Mizraim (Egypt)
nodes.notes: Hebrew/Semitic name for Egypt, cognate with Phoenician Misor (Sanchuniathon) and Coptic/Arabic Misrayim/Baysar.

nodes.name: Phut (Put)
nodes.notes: Jasher 7:12 names his 4 sons: Gebul, Hadan, Benah, and Adan.

nodes.name: Canaan
nodes.notes: Father of 11 Levantine nations including Sidon (Phoenicia), Heth (Hittites), and the Sinites.

nodes.name: Seba
nodes.notes: Son of Cush; linked to Upper Nile / Meroe / Red Sea coast.

nodes.name: Havilah (son of Cush)
nodes.notes: Son of Cush; associated with Red Sea / SW Arabian-African gold lands.

nodes.name: Sabtah
nodes.notes: Son of Cush (often linked to Shabwah in Hadhramaut).

nodes.name: Raamah
nodes.notes: Son of Cush; father of Sheba and Dedan.

nodes.name: Sabteca
nodes.notes: Son of Cush.

nodes.name: Nimrod (Mighty Hunter of Shinar)
nodes.role: King of Babel, Erech (Uruk), Accad & Nineveh
nodes.notes: Crucial Biblical-Mesopotamian bridge: Gen 10:10 links him to Shinar (Sumer), Babel, Erech (Uruk), Accad (Akkad), and Nineveh. Jasher 7:47 names his son Mardon, and Jasher 27 narrates Esau slaying Nimrod!

nodes.name: Sheba (son of Raamah)
nodes.notes: Grandson of Cush via Raamah; Arabian/Red Sea trade lineage.

nodes.name: Dedan (son of Raamah)
nodes.notes: Grandson of Cush via Raamah; NW Arabian oasis of Dedan (Al-Ula).

nodes.name: Mardon (son of Nimrod)
nodes.notes: Named in Book of Jasher 7:47 as Nimrod's son, 'more wicked than his father', origin of the proverb 'from the wicked goeth forth wickedness'.

nodes.name: Ludim
nodes.notes: Descendant of Mizraim; Egyptian/North African archer peoples.

nodes.name: Anamim
nodes.notes: Descendant of Mizraim; Jasher 10:25 places Anamim in Alexandria/coastal Egypt.

nodes.name: Lehabim
nodes.notes: Libyans / western Nile delta peoples.

nodes.name: Naphtuhim
nodes.notes: Lower Egypt / Memphis ('People of Ptah' — Na-Ptah!).

nodes.name: Pathrusim
nodes.notes: Upper Egypt (Egyptian Pa-to-ris, 'the Southland').

nodes.name: Casluhim (→ Philistines)
nodes.notes: Genesis 10:14 notes 'from whom came the Philistines'.

nodes.name: Caphtorim (Crete)
nodes.notes: Historically Keftiu / Minoan Crete, linked to Sea Peoples / Philistines.

nodes.name: Gebul
nodes.notes: Son of Phut listed in Book of Jasher 7:12.

nodes.name: Hadan
nodes.notes: Son of Phut listed in Book of Jasher 7:12.

nodes.name: Benah
nodes.notes: Son of Phut listed in Book of Jasher 7:12.

nodes.name: Adan
nodes.notes: Son of Phut listed in Book of Jasher 7:12.

nodes.name: Sidon (Zidon)
nodes.notes: Firstborn of Canaan; eponym of Phoenician Sidon.

nodes.name: Heth (Hittites)
nodes.notes: Eponym of the Hittites / Children of Heth (from whom Abraham purchased Machpelah).

nodes.name: Jebusite (Jebusi)
nodes.notes: Pre-Israelite inhabitants of Jerusalem (Jebus).

nodes.name: Amorite (Emori)
nodes.notes: Western Semitic Amurru peoples of Syria and Canaan.

nodes.name: Girgashite (Girgashi)
nodes.notes: Canaanite nation listed in Genesis 10:16.

nodes.name: Hivite (Hivi)
nodes.notes: Inhabitants of Shechem, Gibeon, and Mt. Hermon foothills.

nodes.name: Arkite (Arki)
nodes.notes: Ancient city of Arqa in northern Lebanon.

nodes.name: Sinite (Sini)
nodes.notes: Coastal Phoenician city of Sinna/Siannu (later speculated by early European writers as China/Sinim, though historically Levantine).

nodes.name: Arvadite (Arvadi)
nodes.notes: Phoenician island city of Arwad (Syria).

nodes.name: Zemarite (Zemari)
nodes.notes: Ancient Syrian coastal city of Sumur/Simyra.

nodes.name: Hamathite (Hamathi)
nodes.notes: Ancient Syrian kingdom of Hamath (Hama) on the Orontes.

nodes.name: Elam
nodes.notes: Historical kingdom of Elam in SW Iran. Book of Jasher 7:15 names his 3 sons: Shushan (Susa!), Machul, and Harmon.

nodes.name: Asshur
nodes.notes: Historical Assyria. Book of Jasher 7:16 names his 2 sons: Mirus and Mokil.

nodes.name: Arphaxad (Arpachshad)
nodes.notes: Father of Shelach (and Cainan in LXX/Jubilees 8:1). Book of Jasher 7:17 also names his sons Anar and Ashcol.

nodes.name: Lud
nodes.notes: Book of Jasher 7:18 names his 2 sons: Pethor and Bizayon.

nodes.name: Aram
nodes.notes: Father of Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.

nodes.name: Shushan (Susa)
nodes.notes: Son of Elam in Book of Jasher 7:15 — eponym of the historical Elamite capital Susa!

nodes.name: Machul
nodes.notes: Son of Elam in Book of Jasher 7:15.

nodes.name: Harmon
nodes.notes: Son of Elam in Book of Jasher 7:15.

nodes.name: Mirus
nodes.notes: Son of Asshur in Book of Jasher 7:16.

nodes.name: Mokil
nodes.notes: Son of Asshur in Book of Jasher 7:16.

nodes.name: Pethor
nodes.notes: Son of Lud in Book of Jasher 7:18.

nodes.name: Bizayon
nodes.notes: Son of Lud in Book of Jasher 7:18.

nodes.name: Uz (son of Aram)
nodes.notes: Often connected with the Land of Uz (Book of Job) / Damascus region.

nodes.name: Hul
nodes.notes: Son of Aram; linked to Huleh valley or Armenia (Josephus).

nodes.name: Gether
nodes.notes: Son of Aram; linked in Arab tradition to Thamud/Jadhis.

nodes.name: Mash (Meshech)
nodes.notes: Son of Aram; associated with Mount Masius in Upper Mesopotamia.

nodes.name: Cainan (son of Arphaxad)
nodes.notes: Present in Jubilees and Septuagint; Jubilees 8:3 says he discovered an antediluvian rock inscription of the Watchers' astrological teachings.

nodes.name: Shelah (Salah)
nodes.notes: Father of Eber (son of Arphaxad in Masoretic/Jasher; son of Cainan in Jubilees/LXX).

nodes.name: Anar (son of Arphaxad)
nodes.notes: Additional son of Arphaxad listed in Book of Jasher 7:17.

nodes.name: Ashcol (son of Arphaxad)
nodes.notes: Additional son of Arphaxad listed in Book of Jasher 7:17.

nodes.name: Eber (Hud)
nodes.notes: Eponym of the Hebrews and identified in Arabian tradition with Prophet Hud. Father of Peleg and Joktan (Qahtan).

nodes.name: Peleg
nodes.role: Patriarch of the Division of the Earth
nodes.notes: 'In his days the earth was divided' (Tower of Babel). Father of Reu (and Yen in Jasher 7:22).

nodes.name: Joktan (Qahtan)
nodes.notes: Brother of Peleg; father of 13 Arabian tribes spanning from Mesha to Sephar (Yemen/Hadhramaut/Oman). Identified in Arabian genealogy with Qahtan.

nodes.name: Almodad
nodes.notes: 1st of 13 sons of Joktan (Gen 10:26; Jasher 7:21).

nodes.name: Sheleph
nodes.notes: 2nd son of Joktan; linked to Sulaf tribe of Yemen.

nodes.name: Hazarmaveth (Hadhramaut)
nodes.notes: 3rd son of Joktan; exact historical cognate of Hadhramaut in southern Yemen!

nodes.name: Jerah
nodes.notes: 4th son of Joktan; linked to South Arabian lunar sanctuary/tribe.

nodes.name: Hadoram
nodes.notes: 5th son of Joktan.

nodes.name: Uzal (Sana'a)
nodes.notes: 6th son of Joktan; classical ancient name of Sana'a, Yemen!

nodes.name: Diklah
nodes.notes: 7th son of Joktan.

nodes.name: Obal (Ebal)
nodes.notes: 8th son of Joktan (Ebal in 1 Chr 1:22).

nodes.name: Abimael
nodes.notes: 9th son of Joktan.

nodes.name: Sheba / Saba (son of Joktan)
nodes.notes: 10th son of Joktan; linked to the Sabaean Kingdom of Yemen (Queen of Sheba / Makeda!).

nodes.name: Ophir
nodes.notes: 11th son of Joktan; famed ancient source of gold (1 Kings 9:28).

nodes.name: Havilah (son of Joktan)
nodes.notes: 12th son of Joktan; Arabian gold/myrrh region.

nodes.name: Jobab
nodes.notes: 13th son of Joktan.

nodes.name: Yen (son of Peleg)
nodes.notes: Additional son of Peleg listed alongside Reu in Book of Jasher 7:22.

nodes.name: Reu & Ora
nodes.notes: Jubilees 11:1 names his wife Ora, daughter of Ur (founder of Ur of the Chaldees!).

nodes.name: Serug & Milka
nodes.notes: Jubilees 11:6 notes his original name Seroh and wife Milka; Ur/Haran region (Saruj).

nodes.name: Nahor I & Iyaska
nodes.notes: Jubilees 11:9 names his wife Iyaska, daughter of Nestag of the Chaldeans.

nodes.name: Terah & Amthelo / Edna
nodes.role: Father of Abraham, Nahor II & Haran
nodes.notes: Jasher 7:49 names his wife Amthelo daughter of Cornebo (Jubilees 11:14 names Edna). Jasher portrays Terah as captain of Nimrod's host in Shinar before departing Ur for Haran.

nodes.name: Abraham (Abram)
nodes.role: Common Patriarch of Israelites, Ishmaelites, Edomites & Midianites
nodes.notes: Fathers 8 sons across three wives: Isaac (Sarah), Ishmael (Hagar), and Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, Shuah (Keturah). Josephus & Artapanus say Abraham taught astronomy and mathematics in Egypt.

nodes.name: Nahor II & Milcah / Reumah
nodes.role: Brother of Abraham / Grandfather of Rebekah, Leah & Rachel
nodes.notes: Fathers 8 sons by Milcah (including Bethuel -> Rebekah & Laban) and 4 children by Reumah.

nodes.name: Haran (brother of Abraham)
nodes.notes: Died in Ur of the Chaldees (Jasher 12 says he died in Nimrod's furnace). Father of Lot, Milcah, and Sarai/Iscah (Jasher 9:3).

nodes.name: Lot
nodes.notes: Nephew of Abraham; rescued from Sodom. Father of Moab and Ben-Ammi (Ammon).

nodes.name: Milcah
nodes.notes: Daughter of Haran; marries her uncle Nahor II (mother of Bethuel).

nodes.name: Sarah (Sarai / Iscah)
nodes.notes: Wife of Abraham and mother of Isaac. Book of Jasher 9:3 and Talmud Megillah 14a identify her as Haran's daughter Iscah.

nodes.name: Moab (Moabites)
nodes.notes: Progenitor of the Moabites (ancestors of Ruth, great-grandmother of King David!).

nodes.name: Ben-Ammi (Ammonites)
nodes.notes: Progenitor of the Ammonites (centered at Rabbah / modern Amman).

nodes.name: Uz (son of Nahor)
nodes.notes: Firstborn of Nahor II & Milcah (Gen 22:21).

nodes.name: Buz
nodes.notes: Son of Nahor II & Milcah; eponym of Elihu the Buzite in Job.

nodes.name: Kemuel (father of Aram)
nodes.notes: Son of Nahor II & Milcah; father of Aram (Gen 22:21).

nodes.name: Chesed (Chaldeans?)
nodes.notes: Son of Nahor II & Milcah; often linked to the Kasdim/Chaldeans.

nodes.name: Hazo
nodes.notes: Son of Nahor II & Milcah.

nodes.name: Pildash
nodes.notes: Son of Nahor II & Milcah.

nodes.name: Jidlaph
nodes.notes: Son of Nahor II & Milcah.

nodes.name: Bethuel
nodes.notes: Son of Nahor II & Milcah; father of Rebekah (wife of Isaac) and Laban (father of Leah & Rachel).

nodes.name: Tebah
nodes.notes: Son of Nahor II & Reumah (Gen 22:24).

nodes.name: Gaham

nodes.name: Maacah (child of Nahor)
nodes.notes: Child of Nahor II & Reumah (Gen 22:24); eponym of Aramean Maacah.

nodes.name: Rebekah (Rivkah)
nodes.notes: Marries Isaac; mother of Esau and Jacob.

nodes.name: Laban
nodes.notes: Father of Leah and Rachel (wives of Jacob).

nodes.name: Ishmael (Isma'il)
nodes.role: Firstborn of Abraham (via Hagar) / Father of 12 Princes
nodes.notes: Jasher 21 names his wives Meribah (divorced) and Malchuth of Egypt. Fathers 12 Arabian tribal princes and daughter Mahalath/Basemath (who marries Esau).

nodes.name: Nebaioth (Nabit)
nodes.notes: 1st son of Ishmael; attested as Nabayati in Neo-Assyrian inscriptions and linked to Nabataeans / Adnanite lineage.

nodes.name: Kedar (Qaydar)
nodes.notes: 2nd son of Ishmael; attested as the Qedarite Kingdom (Qidri) in Neo-Assyrian records; traditional ancestor of Adnan & Quraysh.

nodes.name: Adbeel
nodes.notes: 3rd son of Ishmael; attested as Idibi'ilu in Tiglath-Pileser III annals.

nodes.name: Mibsam
nodes.notes: 4th son of Ishmael.

nodes.name: Mishma
nodes.notes: 5th son of Ishmael.

nodes.name: Dumah
nodes.notes: 6th son of Ishmael; oasis of Dumat al-Jandal (Adummatu) in Northern Arabia.

nodes.name: Massa
nodes.notes: 7th son of Ishmael; North Arabian tribe of Mas'a.

nodes.name: Hadad (Hadar)
nodes.notes: 8th son of Ishmael.

nodes.name: Tema (Tayma)
nodes.notes: 9th son of Ishmael; famous NW Arabian caravan oasis of Tayma.

nodes.name: Jetur (Ituraeans)
nodes.notes: 10th son of Ishmael; Ituraean tribes of northern Transjordan/Lebanon.

nodes.name: Naphish
nodes.notes: 11th son of Ishmael.

nodes.name: Kedemah
nodes.notes: 12th son of Ishmael.

nodes.name: Mahalath / Basemath (dau. of Ishmael)
nodes.notes: Sister of Nebaioth; marries her cousin Esau, uniting Ishmaelite and Edomite lines!

nodes.name: Adnan → Ma'add → Nizar → Quraysh → Muhammad
nodes.notes: Classical Arabian genealogies trace the Northern Arabs from Ishmael (via Kedar/Nebaioth) through Adnan -> Ma'add -> Nizar -> Mudar -> Fihr (Quraysh) -> Qusayy -> Abd Manaf -> Hashim -> Abd al-Muttalib -> Abdullah -> Muhammad.

nodes.name: Zimran
nodes.notes: 1st son of Abraham & Keturah. Jasher 25:3 names his 3 sons: Abihen, Molich, Narim.

nodes.name: Jokshan
nodes.notes: 2nd son of Abraham & Keturah; father of Sheba and Dedan.

nodes.name: Medan
nodes.notes: 3rd son of Abraham & Keturah. Jasher 25:4 names his 5 sons: Amida, Joab, Gochi, Elisha, Nothach.

nodes.name: Midian
nodes.notes: 4th son of Abraham & Keturah; father of Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, Eldaah. Ancestor of Reuel/Jethro and Moses's wife Zipporah.

nodes.name: Ishbak
nodes.notes: 5th son of Abraham & Keturah. Jasher 25:5 names his 3 sons: Makiro, Beydod, Tator.

nodes.name: Shuah
nodes.notes: 6th son of Abraham & Keturah; eponym of Shuhites (Bildad in Job). Jasher 25:5 names his 4 sons: Bildad, Mamdad, Munan, Meban.

nodes.name: Abihen
nodes.notes: Son of Zimran in Book of Jasher 25:3.

nodes.name: Molich
nodes.notes: Son of Zimran in Book of Jasher 25:3.

nodes.name: Narim
nodes.notes: Son of Zimran in Book of Jasher 25:3.

nodes.name: Sheba (son of Jokshan)
nodes.notes: Grandson of Abraham via Jokshan (Northern Sabaean trade network).

nodes.name: Dedan (son of Jokshan)
nodes.notes: Grandson of Abraham via Jokshan; father of Asshurim, Letushim, Leummim.

nodes.name: Asshurim
nodes.notes: Descendant tribe of Abraham via Jokshan -> Dedan (Gen 25:3).

nodes.name: Letushim

nodes.name: Leummim

nodes.notes: Midianite priest (Shu'ayb in Islamic tradition) who shelters Moses after his reign in Cush (Jasher 76) and gives him his daughter Zipporah.

nodes.name: Isaac (Yitzhak) & Rebekah
nodes.notes: Marries Rebekah (daughter of Bethuel, granddaughter of Nahor II). Father of twin sons Esau (Edom) and Jacob (Israel).

nodes.name: Esau (Edom)
nodes.notes: Marries Adah (Hittite), Oholibamah (Hivite/Horite), and Basemath/Mahalath (daughter of Ishmael). Jasher 27 narrates Esau slaying Nimrod and taking Adam's garments!

nodes.name: Eliphaz
nodes.notes: Firstborn of Esau (via Adah); father of Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, Kenaz, and Amalek (via Timna).

nodes.name: Reuel (son of Esau)
nodes.notes: Son of Esau & Basemath (daughter of Ishmael) — uniting Edom and Ishmael! Father of Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, Mizzah.

nodes.name: Jeush
nodes.notes: Son of Esau & Oholibamah (daughter of Anah the Horite).

nodes.name: Jalam
nodes.notes: Son of Esau & Oholibamah.

nodes.name: Korah (son of Esau)
nodes.notes: Son of Esau & Oholibamah.

nodes.name: Teman
nodes.notes: Eponym of Teman in Edom (linked to Eliphaz the Temanite in Job).

nodes.name: Omar
nodes.notes: Son of Eliphaz (Gen 36:11).

nodes.name: Zepho (King of Kittim / Italy)
nodes.role: Traditional Jasher Bridge from Edom to Italy/Rome
nodes.notes: In Book of Jasher ch. 57-61, Zepho escapes Joseph's prison in Egypt, flees to Kittim (Italy), slays a beast and defeats Angeas king of Africa, and becomes King of Chittim (father of Janeus/Janus)!

nodes.name: Gatam
nodes.notes: Son of Eliphaz (Gen 36:11).

nodes.name: Kenaz
nodes.notes: Son of Eliphaz (Gen 36:11); linked to the Kenizzites.

nodes.name: Amalek (Amalekites)
nodes.notes: Son of Eliphaz & Timna (sister of Lotan the Horite); ancestor of the Amalekites.

nodes.name: Nahath
nodes.notes: Son of Reuel (Gen 36:13).

nodes.name: Zerah (son of Reuel)
nodes.notes: Son of Reuel (Gen 36:13); father of Jobab king of Edom (Gen 36:33).

nodes.name: Shammah

nodes.name: Mizzah

nodes.name: Janeus (Janus of Italy)
nodes.notes: Son of Zepho in Book of Jasher 62:25, succeeding him as king over Kittim (Italy) — echoing Roman Janus!

nodes.notes: Marries Leah and Rachel (daughters of Laban) plus Bilhah and Zilpah. Fathers 12 sons and daughter Dinah, with all 70 household members enumerated in Genesis 46 & Jasher 59.

nodes.name: Izhar

nodes.name: Miriam
nodes.notes: Prophetess, sister of Moses and Aaron.

nodes.name: Aaron (High Priest)
nodes.notes: First High Priest of Israel; marries Elisheba (father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, Ithamar).

nodes.name: Moses (Moshe)
nodes.role: Lawgiver / Prince of Egypt / King of Cush (Jasher)
nodes.notes: Raised by Pharaoh's daughter Bithiah (1 Chr 4:18; Jasher 68). Book of Jasher 72-76 (and Josephus Ant. 2.10) recounts Moses serving as King of Cush (Ethiopia) for 40 years with Queen Adoniah before marrying Zipporah in Midian! Identified in Manetho as Egyptian priest Osarseph and in Artapanus as Musaeus/Hermes.

nodes.name: Gershom (son of Moses)
nodes.notes: Firstborn son of Moses & Zipporah (daughter of Jethro of Midian).

nodes.name: Eliezer (son of Moses)
nodes.notes: Second son of Moses & Zipporah.

nodes.name: Er
nodes.notes: 1st son of Judah & Shua's daughter (Gen 38:3).

nodes.name: Onan
nodes.notes: 2nd son of Judah (Gen 38:4).

nodes.name: Shelah (son of Judah)
nodes.notes: 3rd son of Judah (Gen 38:5).

nodes.name: Zerah (son of Judah)
nodes.notes: Twin son of Judah & Tamar (Gen 38:30); linked in some classical/Irish traditions to Mediterranean migrations.

nodes.name: Perez (Pharez)
nodes.notes: Twin son of Judah & Tamar; direct ancestor of Boaz, King David, and the royal Davidic line.

nodes.name: Hezron → Ram → Nahshon → Boaz (+ Ruth) → Jesse
nodes.role: Bridge from Perez to Davidic Dynasty (Uniting Judah & Moab)
nodes.notes: Boaz marries Ruth the Moabitess (descendant of Lot!), uniting the Israelite line of Judah with the Moabite line of Lot.

nodes.name: King David
nodes.role: King of Israel & Founder of Davidic Dynasty
nodes.notes: Son of Jesse; father of Solomon, Absalom, Adonijah, Nathan, and Tamar.

nodes.name: King Solomon (Shlomo)
nodes.notes: Father of Rehoboam (Judah). In Ethiopia's national epic Kebra Nagast, Solomon and Makeda (Queen of Sheba) parent Menelik I, bridging Israel, Arabia/Sheba, and Ethiopia!

nodes.name: Menelik I (Solomonic Dynasty of Ethiopia)
nodes.notes: Son of King Solomon and Queen Makeda of Sheba (Saba). Creates a famous African-Arabian-Israelite royal genealogy bridging Cush/Ethiopia, Sheba, and Judah!

nodes.name: Manasseh (son of Joseph)
nodes.notes: Firstborn of Joseph & Asenath (daughter of Poti-phera, Priest of On).

nodes.name: Ephraim (son of Joseph)
nodes.notes: Second son of Joseph & Asenath; ancestor of Joshua.

nodes.name: Atum → Shu/Tefnut → Geb/Nut → Osiris & Isis → Horus
nodes.notes: Egyptian royal king lists trace historical pharaohs directly from the Ennead and Horus through the Shemsu-Hor ('Followers of Horus'). Osiris placed in a chest/ark on the Nile was later compared by syncretists to Noah.

nodes.name: Thoth (Djehuty / Hermes) & King Saurid (Surid)
nodes.role: Egyptian Scribe of the Gods / Antediluvian Pyramid Builder
nodes.notes: Greco-Egyptian, Hermetic, Coptic, and Arabic histories explicitly identify Biblical Enoch (Idris) with Egyptian Thoth / Hermes Trismegistus and the antediluvian Egyptian King Saurid (Surid), who foresaw the Flood and built the Pyramids to preserve astronomy and sacred wisdom!

nodes.name: Menes / Narmer (1st Dynasty) & Baysar (Misrayim)
nodes.notes: Historical unifier of Egypt. Medieval Coptic/Arabic chronicles (al-Maqrizi) trace post-Flood Egyptian kings from Ham -> Baysar -> Misrayim (Mizraim), while Book of Jasher 14 recounts Rikayon establishing the royal title 'Pharaoh'!

nodes.name: Imhotep (Vizier of Djoser / 7-Year Famine)
nodes.era: Old Kingdom (3rd Dynasty) / Ptolemaic Famine Stela
nodes.notes: Master architect of the Step Pyramid and high priest of Heliopolis (On). The Sehel Island Famine Stela credits Imhotep with ending a 7-year Nile famine—frequently compared in cross-cultural lore with Joseph (Zaphenath-Paneah), who wed the daughter of the Priest of On!

nodes.name: Osarseph (Manetho) / Musaeus (Artapanus) / Bithiah & Adoniah
nodes.notes: Manetho preserves an Egyptian tradition of a Heliopolitan priest named Osarseph who took the name Moses; Artapanus calls Moses 'Musaeus' (teacher of Orpheus) and Egyptian 'Hermes', leading an expedition into Cush/Ethiopia — strikingly echoing Book of Jasher 72-76 where Moses rules Cush with Queen Adoniah!

nodes.name: Protogonos → Misor & Sydyk → Taaut (Thoth) & Chna (Canaan)
sources: Philo of Byblos / Sanchuniathon (via Eusebius Praep. Ev. I.10)
nodes.notes: Explicitly names Misor (direct cognate of Biblical Mizraim!) as brother of Sydyk (Righteousness, cf. Melchizedek) and father of Taaut (Egyptian Thoth, inventor of writing), alongside Chna (Canaan).

nodes.name: Apsu & Tiamat
nodes.notes: Primordial cosmic waters whose mingling generates the elder gods Lahmu and Lahamu.

nodes.name: Lahmu & Lahamu
nodes.notes: Born of Apsu & Tiamat; parents of Anshar & Kishar.

nodes.name: Anshar & Kishar
nodes.notes: Parents of the Sky Father Anu.

nodes.name: Anu (An) & Antu / Ki
nodes.notes: Supreme sky deity of Uruk; father of Enki (Ea) and Enlil.

nodes.name: Enki (Ea) & Damkina (Ninhursag)
nodes.role: Creator of Humanity & Protector of Flood Survivor
nodes.notes: Patron of Eridu; with Nintu/Belet-ili fashions the first humans (Lullu) from clay mixed with divine blood, and secretly warns Ziusudra/Atrahasis of the Flood.

nodes.name: Enlil & Ninlil
nodes.notes: Father of Nanna (Sin) and Ninurta; decrees the Deluge in Atrahasis.

nodes.name: Marduk (Bel)
nodes.notes: Son of Enki (Ea) & Damkina; slays Tiamat, builds Babylon, and fashions humanity from Qingu's blood.

nodes.name: Nabu (Scribe God of Borsippa)
nodes.notes: Son of Marduk; keeper of the Tablets of Destiny and patron of scribes.

nodes.name: Ninurta (Ningirsu)
nodes.notes: Mythic hunter and champion of the gods — widely proposed by Assyriologists as a mythological source for Biblical Nimrod ('mighty hunter')!

nodes.name: Nanna (Sin — Moon God of Ur)
nodes.notes: Moon god of Ur; marries Ningal and fathers Utu (Shamash) and Inanna (Ishtar).

nodes.name: Utu (Shamash — Sun God of Sippar/Larsa)
nodes.notes: Son of Nanna; reveals celestial tablets to 7th king Enmeduranki at Sippar and fathers Meskiaggasher of Uruk!

nodes.name: Inanna (Ishtar — Queen of Heaven)
nodes.notes: Patron goddess of Uruk (Eanna) and consort of Dumuzid.

nodes.name: Lullu (First Humans) & Adapa / Uanna (1st Apkallu)
nodes.notes: Lullu is fashioned from clay + divine blood of We-ilu/Qingu. Adapa (1st Apkallu sage under Alulim, called Oannes by Berossus) ascends to heaven and forfeits eternal life — widely compared to Adam!

nodes.name: 1. Alulim (Aloros of Eridu)
nodes.notes: 1st Antediluvian King of Eridu; advised by 1st Apkallu sage Uanna/Adapa.

nodes.name: 2. Alalngar (Alaparos of Eridu)
nodes.notes: 2nd Antediluvian King of Eridu; sage Uannedugga.

nodes.name: 3. En-men-lu-ana (Amelon of Bad-tibira)
nodes.notes: 3rd Antediluvian King; kingship moves to Bad-tibira; sage Enmedugga.

nodes.name: 4. En-men-gal-ana (Ammenon of Bad-tibira)
nodes.notes: 4th Antediluvian King of Bad-tibira; sage Enmegalamma.

nodes.name: 5. Dumuzid the Shepherd (Daonos)
nodes.notes: 5th Antediluvian King of Bad-tibira; sage Enmebulugga.

nodes.name: 6. En-sipad-zid-ana (Amempsinos of Larak)
nodes.notes: 6th Antediluvian King; kingship moves to Larak; sage An-Enlilda.

nodes.name: 7. En-men-dur-ana (Enmeduranki of Sippar)
nodes.notes: 7th Antediluvian King (Euedorachos in Berossus); ruler of sun-city Sippar, initiated by Shamash & Adad into heavenly secrets and divination alongside 7th sage Utuabzu (who ascends to heaven) — exact structural parallel to Enoch (7th patriarch, 365 solar years)!

nodes.name: 8. Megalaros / Amegalaros (Berossus)
nodes.notes: Included in Berossus's 10-king antediluvian list (matching Genesis 5's 10 patriarchs).

nodes.name: 9. Ubara-Tutu (Otiartes of Shuruppak)
nodes.notes: Last king of Shuruppak before the Deluge; father of Ziusudra / Utnapishtim!

nodes.name: 10. Ziusudra / Utnapishtim / Atrahasis
nodes.notes: 10th Antediluvian ruler (Xisouthros in Berossus). Warned by Enki/Ea of the Deluge; builds a vessel preserving family and animals; releases dove, swallow, and raven; lands on Mt. Nimush.

nodes.name: Utuabzu (7th Apkallu Sage Who Ascended to Heaven)
nodes.notes: The 7th antediluvian sage, counselor to 7th king Enmeduranki, explicitly recorded as 'having ascended to heaven' — a stunning Mesopotamian parallel to Enoch (7th from Adam, taken to heaven)!

nodes.name: Jushur (1st Post-Flood King of Kish)
nodes.notes: First king after the Flood swept over and kingship descended from heaven anew at Kish.

nodes.name: Kullassina-bel
nodes.notes: 2nd king of Kish I ('All of them were lord').

nodes.name: Nangishlishma
nodes.notes: 3rd king of Kish I.

nodes.name: En-tarah-ana
nodes.notes: 4th king of Kish I.

nodes.name: Puannum

nodes.name: Kalibum

nodes.notes: 9th king of Kish I.

nodes.name: Atab
nodes.notes: 10th king of Kish I.

nodes.name: Mashda (son of Atab)
nodes.notes: 11th king of Kish I; son of Atab.

nodes.name: Arwium (son of Mashda)
nodes.notes: 12th king of Kish I; son of Mashda.

nodes.name: Etana of Kish (Ascended on an Eagle)
nodes.notes: 13th king of Kish I; 'the shepherd who ascended to heaven and consolidated all foreign countries' on an eagle's back to obtain the Plant of Birth.

nodes.name: Balih (son of Etana)
nodes.notes: 14th king of Kish I; son of Etana.

nodes.name: En-me-nuna
nodes.notes: 15th king of Kish I; father of Melem-Kish and Barsal-nuna.

nodes.name: Melem-Kish (son of En-me-nuna)
nodes.notes: 16th king of Kish I.

nodes.name: Barsal-nuna (son of En-me-nuna)
nodes.notes: 17th king of Kish I.

nodes.name: Zamug (son of Barsal-nuna)
nodes.notes: 18th king of Kish I.

nodes.name: Tizqar (son of Zamug)
nodes.notes: 19th king of Kish I.

nodes.name: Ilku
nodes.notes: 20th king of Kish I.

nodes.name: Iltasadum
nodes.notes: 21st king of Kish I.

nodes.name: Enmebaragesi of Kish (Conqueror of Elam)
nodes.era: First Dynasty of Kish • c. 2600 BCE
nodes.notes: 22nd king of Kish I; earliest Sumerian king confirmed by contemporary inscriptions! 'Carried away as spoil the weapons of Elam'.

nodes.name: Aga (Agga) of Kish
nodes.era: First Dynasty of Kish • c. 2600 BCE
nodes.notes: 23rd and final king of Kish I; son of Enmebaragesi, besieged Uruk and clashed with Gilgamesh.

nodes.name: Meskiaggasher (Founder of Uruk / Erech)
nodes.role: Son of Sun God Utu (Shamash) / 1st King of Uruk
nodes.notes: High priest and king of Eanna; 'entered the sea and ascended to the mountains'. Father of Enmerkar.

nodes.name: Enmerkar (Builder of Uruk / Erech)
nodes.role: 2nd King of Uruk / Inventor of Cuneiform
sources: Enmerkar and the Lord of Aratta
nodes.notes: Son of Meskiaggasher; built Uruk (Biblical Erech, Gen 10:10) and invented cuneiform clay tablets in rivalry with Aratta (Iranian plateau!). Widely compared to Nimrod ('Enmer the Hunter').

nodes.name: Lugalbanda & Goddess Ninsun
nodes.role: 3rd King of Uruk / Father of Gilgamesh
nodes.notes: Companion of Enmerkar; weds goddess Ninsun and fathers Gilgamesh.

nodes.name: Dumuzid the Fisherman (of Kuara)
nodes.notes: Captured Enmebaragesi of Kish single-handedly before Gilgamesh.

nodes.name: Gilgamesh (Bilgamesh of Uruk / Erech)
nodes.role: 5th King of Uruk / Builder of Uruk's Walls / Qumran Giant
nodes.notes: Son of Lugalbanda & Ninsun; visits Flood survivor Utnapishtim. Uruk is explicitly 'Erech' in Gen 10:10 — and 'Gilgamesh' is literally named as a Giant in Qumran Book of Giants (4Q530)!

nodes.name: Ur-Nungal (son of Gilgamesh)
nodes.notes: 6th king of Uruk I; son of Gilgamesh (reigned 30 yrs).

nodes.name: Udul-kalama (son of Ur-Nungal)
nodes.notes: 7th king of Uruk I; grandson of Gilgamesh (15 yrs).

nodes.name: La-ba'shum
nodes.notes: 8th king of Uruk I (9 yrs).

nodes.name: En-nun-tarah-ana
nodes.notes: 9th king of Uruk I (8 yrs).

nodes.name: Mesh-he
nodes.notes: 10th king of Uruk I (36 yrs).

nodes.name: Melem-ana
nodes.notes: 11th king of Uruk I (6 yrs).

nodes.name: Lugal-kitun
nodes.notes: 12th and final king of Uruk I (36 yrs).

nodes.name: Mesannepada (Founder of Ur I)
nodes.role: 1st King of First Dynasty of Ur
nodes.notes: Overthrew Uruk I; attested by royal seals from Ur.

nodes.name: Mesh-ki-ang-nanna (son of Mesannepada)
nodes.notes: Son of Mesannepada; followed by Elulu and Balulu.

nodes.name: Sargon of Akkad (Sharru-kin)
nodes.notes: Cupbearer of Ur-Zababa of Kish who founded the world's first empire (Biblical Accad, Gen 10:10). His Birth Legend ('reed basket sealed with bitumen on the river') parallels Moses in Exodus 2!

nodes.name: Enheduanna (High Priestess of Ur)
nodes.role: Daughter of Sargon / Earliest Named Author in History
nodes.notes: Daughter of Sargon of Akkad appointed High Priestess of Nanna at Ur; world's earliest known named author!

nodes.name: Rimush (son of Sargon)
nodes.notes: Son of Sargon; campaigned against rebellious Sumerian cities and Elam.

nodes.name: Manishtushu (son of Sargon)
nodes.notes: Son of Sargon; father of Naram-Sin.

nodes.name: Naram-Sin ('King of the Four Quarters')
nodes.notes: Son of Manishtushu; peak of Akkadian Empire.

nodes.name: Shar-Kali-Sharri (son of Naram-Sin)
nodes.notes: Son of Naram-Sin; reigned as the Akkadian Empire faced Gutian invasions.

nodes.name: Ur-Nammu (Founder of Ur III — Ur of the Chaldees)
nodes.role: Builder of Great Ziggurat / Oldest Law Code
nodes.notes: Founded Ur III and issued history's oldest surviving law code — the exact historical era of Ur of the Chaldees before Terah & Abraham's migration (Gen 11:31)!

nodes.name: Shulgi (son of Ur-Nammu)
nodes.notes: Son of Ur-Nammu; reigned 48 years, standardized weights, measures, and scribal academies.

nodes.name: Amar-Sin (son of Shulgi)
nodes.notes: Son of Shulgi.

nodes.name: Shu-Sin (brother/son of Amar-Sin)
nodes.notes: Built the Martu Wall to hold back western Amorite tribes.

nodes.name: Ibbi-Sin (Last King of Ur III)
nodes.role: 5th King of Ur III (Fall of Ur to Elam)
nodes.notes: Ur fell to Elamite and Shimashki invaders in 2004 BCE — matching the historical backdrop of Terah & Abraham leaving Ur!

nodes.name: Sumu-abum → Sumu-la-El → Sin-Muballit (Early Babylon)
nodes.notes: Amorite chieftains who established the First Dynasty of Babylon: Sumu-abum -> Sumu-la-El -> Sabium -> Apil-Sin -> Sin-Muballit (father of Hammurabi).

nodes.name: Hammurabi of Babylon (→ Samsu-iluna)
nodes.notes: 6th king of the Amorite Dynasty of Babylon; unified Mesopotamia and issued the Code of Hammurabi. Father of Samsu-iluna.

nodes.name: Tudiya → Ushpia → Shamshi-Adad I → Tukulti-Ninurta I → Ashurbanipal
nodes.notes: Begins with '17 Kings Who Lived in Tents' (Tudiya -> Ushpia) and leads to Tukulti-Ninurta I (often cited as a historical prototype for Nimrod!), Sennacherib, and Ashurbanipal (whose library preserved Gilgamesh & Enuma Elish!).

nodes.name: Gayomart (Gaya Maretan / Keyumars)
nodes.role: First Mortal Human & First Pishdadian King
nodes.notes: Created by Ahura Mazda ('Mortal Life'). From his seed purified in the earth grew a rhubarb plant splitting into Mashya and Mashyana.

nodes.name: Mashya & Mashyana
nodes.role: First Human Couple (7 Pairs of Twins)
nodes.notes: Twin first man and woman who bore 7 pairs of twins, including Siamak & Nashak (ancestors of Iran) and Fravak & Fravakain (ancestors of all 15 human races!).

nodes.name: Fravak & Fravakain (Zoroastrian Table of Nations)
nodes.role: Progenitors of the 15 Races Across 7 Climes
nodes.notes: Bundahishn Ch. 14 traces 15 distinct human nations across the 7 climes (karshvars) to Fravak & Fravakain — including Iranians (Hoshang), Arabs (Taz), Mazandaran, India, Turan, China (Chin), and the West (Rum)!

nodes.name: Taz & Tazag (Arabs / Taziks)
nodes.notes: Son of Fravak; eponym of the Arabian peoples (Middle Persian Tazig) and ancestor of Merdas -> Zahhak!

nodes.name: Mazandarani (Caspian Lineage)
nodes.notes: One of the races descended from Fravak in Bundahishn Ch. 14.

nodes.name: Hindug (Indians in Bundahishn)
nodes.notes: Branch of humanity settling India from Fravak's 15 pairs.

nodes.name: Chin (China in Bundahishn)
nodes.notes: Branch of humanity settling East Asia/China in Zoroastrian ethnography.

nodes.name: Arum / Rum (Western Peoples)
nodes.notes: Branch settling the western Mediterranean/Anatolian clime.

nodes.name: Merdas (Arabian King, desc. of Taz)
nodes.notes: Pious Arabian king descended from Taz, slain by his own son Zahhak under Ahriman's deception.

nodes.name: Zahhak (Azi Dahaka)
nodes.role: Dragon Usurper King of Babylon & Iran
nodes.notes: Son of Merdas; overthrows Jamshid and rules 1,000 years from Bawri (Babylon!) before being bound on Mt. Damavand by Fereydun. Ancestor of Mehrab Kaboli -> Rudabeh (mother of Rostam!).

nodes.name: Siamak & Nashak
nodes.notes: Slain by the Black Div; avenged by his son Hushang.

nodes.name: Hushang (Haoshyangha) & Guzak
nodes.notes: Founder of the Pishdadian ('First Lawgivers') dynasty; establishes Sadeh upon discovering fire.

nodes.name: Tahmuras (Takhma Urupi)
nodes.notes: Binds Ahriman for 30 years and learns 30 scripts from captive demons to teach humanity.

nodes.name: Vivanghant (Vivanhao)
nodes.notes: EXACT Proto-Indo-Iranian linguistic & genealogical cognate of Vedic Vivasvan (Surya)! Strongest verified prehistoric ancestral bridge between Iran and India.

nodes.name: Yima Khshaeta (Jamshid) & Yimak
nodes.role: 4th Pishdadian King & Builder of the Vara
nodes.notes: Son of Vivanghant — exact cognate of Vedic Yama! Builds the subterranean Vara preserving pairs of humans, animals, and seeds against the great cosmic winter/meltwater cataclysm.

nodes.name: Shahrnaz & Arnavaz (Daughters of Jamshid)
nodes.role: Wives of Fereydun / Mothers of Salm, Tur & Iraj
nodes.notes: Daughters/sisters of Jamshid rescued from Zahhak by Fereydun; Shahrnaz bears Salm & Tur, and Arnavaz bears Iraj!

nodes.name: Athwya (Abtin) & Faranak
nodes.role: Father of Fereydun / Exact Cognate of Vedic Aptya
nodes.notes: Descendant of Jamshid (via Pur-Tora/Sog-Tora in Bundahishn 35); EXACT Proto-Indo-Iranian cognate of Vedic Aptya (father of Trita Aptya)!

nodes.name: Fereydun (Thraetaona)
nodes.role: Binder of Zahhak & Divider of the World Into Three
nodes.notes: Son of Athwya (Abtin) & Faranak — cognate of Vedic Trita! Weds Shahrnaz & Arnavaz, binds Zahhak on Mt. Damavand, and divides the world among Salm, Tur, and Iraj.

nodes.name: Salm (Ruler of the West / Rum)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Fereydun & Shahrnaz; receives Rum/West.

nodes.name: Tur (Ruler of Turan / Central Asia)
nodes.notes: Second son of Fereydun & Shahrnaz; receives Central Asia & Steppe.

nodes.name: Zadsham (son of Tur)
nodes.notes: Father of Pashang.

nodes.name: Pashang (King of Turan)
nodes.notes: Son of Zadsham; launches the great Iran-Turan wars.

nodes.name: Afrasiab (Franrasyan)
nodes.role: Great King of Turan / Grandfather of Kay Khosrow
nodes.notes: Son of Pashang; legendary rival of Iran whose daughter Farangis marries Siyavash, uniting Iran and Turan in Kay Khosrow!

nodes.name: Garsivaz & Aghriras (Brothers of Afrasiab)
nodes.notes: Aghriras (noble brother who saved Iranian captives) and Garsivaz (instigator of Siyavash's murder).

nodes.name: Farangis (Turanian Princess)
nodes.role: Wife of Siyavash / Mother of Kay Khosrow
nodes.notes: Daughter of Afrasiab; marries Iranian prince Siyavash and gives birth to Kay Khosrow, uniting Turan and Iran!

nodes.name: Iraj (Ruler of Iran / Eranshahr)
nodes.role: 3rd Son of Fereydun / Eponym of Iran
nodes.notes: Youngest son of Fereydun & Arnavaz; receives Iran. Slain by Salm & Tur.

nodes.name: Mah-Afarid (Daughter of Iraj)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Iraj wed to Pashang (nephew of Fereydun), preserving Iraj's bloodline into Manuchehr.

nodes.name: Manuchehr (Manushchihr)
nodes.role: Avenger of Iraj / Ancestor of Kayanians & Zoroaster
nodes.notes: Avenges Iraj against Salm & Tur; defines Iran's border via Arash the Archer's legendary shot!

nodes.name: Nowzar (son of Manuchehr)
nodes.notes: Slain by Afrasiab; his sons Tus and Gostaham become leading Iranian generals.

nodes.name: Tus & Gostaham (Sons of Nowzar)
nodes.notes: Sons of Nowzar who serve the Kayanian kings.

nodes.name: Zav (Uzava, son of Tahmasp)
nodes.notes: Descendant of Manuchehr who restores agriculture after Afrasiab's drought.

nodes.name: Garshasp (Keresaspa — Dragon-Slayer)
nodes.notes: Avestan champion and final Pishdadian ruler; ancestor of the Sistan paladins (Nariman -> Sam -> Zal -> Rostam).

nodes.name: Nariman (son of Garshasp)
nodes.notes: Warrior ancestor of the House of Sistan.

nodes.name: Sam (Paladin of Iran)
nodes.notes: Champion under Manuchehr; initially abandoned his white-haired infant Zal on Mt. Alborz before reclaiming him from the Simurgh.

nodes.name: Zal (Dastan — Raised by the Simurgh)
nodes.notes: White-haired sage-warrior raised by the mythical Simurgh; weds Rudabeh of Kabul.

nodes.name: Mehrab Kaboli (King of Kabul)
nodes.role: Descendant of Zahhak / Father of Rudabeh
nodes.notes: Ruler of Kabul descended from Zahhak; father of Rudabeh.

nodes.name: Rudabeh (Princess of Kabul)
nodes.role: Wife of Zal / Mother of Rostam
nodes.notes: Her union with Zal bridges Kabul/Zahhak's line with Iran's greatest heroic house!

nodes.name: Rostam (Champion of Iran)
nodes.notes: Son of Zal & Rudabeh; serves the Kayanian kings for centuries. Marries Tahmineh of Samangan (Turan) -> Sohrab, plus Faramarz and warrior daughter Banu Goshasp.

nodes.name: Shaghad (Half-Brother of Rostam)
nodes.notes: Rostam's treacherous half-brother who conspires with the King of Kabul.

nodes.name: Sohrab (son of Rostam & Tahmineh)
nodes.role: Son of Rostam & Turanian Princess Tahmineh
nodes.notes: Born in Samangan (Turan); tragically slain in single combat by his father Rostam before they recognize one another.

nodes.name: Faramarz & Banu Goshasp (Children of Rostam)
nodes.notes: Faramarz leads expeditions into India and avenges Rostam; Banu Goshasp is a celebrated Iranian warrior heroine.

nodes.name: Kay Kavad (Kavi Kavata)
nodes.notes: Descendant of Manuchehr brought from Mt. Alborz by Rostam; father of Kay Kavus and Kay Apiveh.

nodes.name: Kay Apiveh → Kay Arash & Kay Pishin
nodes.notes: Branch of Kay Kavad leading to Kay Lohrasp and Kay Goshtasp (patron of Zoroaster).

nodes.name: Kay Kavus (Kavi Usan)
nodes.notes: Linguistic cognate of Vedic sage Kavi Ushanas! Father of Prince Siyavash.

nodes.name: Siyavash (Syavarshan)
nodes.role: Son of Kay Kavus / Husband of Farangis
nodes.notes: Passes through fire unscathed; weds Afrasiab's daughter Farangis in Turan; father of Kay Khosrow and Farud.

nodes.name: Farud (son of Siyavash & Jarireh)
nodes.notes: Son of Siyavash and Jarireh (daughter of Turanian sage Piran Viseh).

nodes.name: Kay Khosrow (Kavi Husravah)
nodes.role: Ideal Sacred King of Avesta & Shahnameh
nodes.notes: Son of Siyavash (Iran) & Farangis (Turan); unites both houses, defeats Afrasiab, and passes the crown to Kay Lohrasp.

nodes.name: Kay Lohrasp (Aurvat-aspa)
nodes.notes: Descended from Kay Apiveh -> Kay Pishin -> Kay Lohrasp; builds the fire temple at Balkh.

nodes.name: Kay Goshtasp (Kavi Vishtaspa)
nodes.notes: Champions Prophet Zarathustra's religion; father of hero Esfandiyar and brother Zarir.

nodes.name: Esfandiyar (Spento-data)
nodes.role: Son of Kay Goshtasp / Father of Bahman
nodes.notes: Bronze-bodied champion of Zoroastrianism slain by Rostam's tamarisk arrow; father of Kay Bahman.

nodes.name: Kay Bahman → Queen Homai → Darab → Dara
nodes.role: Bridge to Historical Artaxerxes & Darius III
nodes.notes: Kay Bahman (equated in Persian lore with Artaxerxes Longimanus) -> Queen Homai -> Darab -> Dara (Darius III, rival of Alexander!).

nodes.name: Spitama → Haechataspa → Pourushaspa & Dughdova
nodes.notes: Bundahishn traces Spitama (descended from Manuchehr) -> Haechataspa -> Pourushaspa, who marries Dughdova to birth Zarathustra.

nodes.name: Prophet Zarathustra (Zoroaster) & Hvovi
nodes.notes: Author of the Gathas; weds Hvovi (of the Hvova clan, kin of Frashaoshtra & Jamaspa) and fathers 3 sons and 3 daughters.

nodes.name: Isatvastra (son of Zarathustra)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Zarathustra; head of the priestly estate (Athornan).

nodes.name: Urvatatnara (son of Zarathustra)
nodes.notes: Son of Zarathustra; head of the pastoral/agricultural estate.

nodes.name: Hvarechithra (son of Zarathustra)
nodes.notes: Son of Zarathustra; head of the warrior estate.

nodes.name: Freni (dau. of Zarathustra)
nodes.notes: 1st daughter of Zarathustra.

nodes.name: Thriti (dau. of Zarathustra)
nodes.notes: 2nd daughter of Zarathustra.

nodes.name: Pouruchista (+ Jamaspa)
nodes.notes: Youngest daughter of Zarathustra celebrated in Gatha Yasna 53; marries sage Jamaspa (counselor of King Vishtaspa).

nodes.name: Deioces → Phraortes (Early Medes)
nodes.role: Founders of the Median Kingdom (Biblical Madai)
nodes.notes: Deioces (Dayukku) unifies the Median tribes at Ecbatana; followed by his son Phraortes.

nodes.name: Cyaxares (Uvakhshatra) → Astyages
nodes.role: Conquerors of Nineveh / Kings of Media
nodes.notes: Cyaxares destroys Nineveh (612 BCE) in alliance with Babylon; his son Astyages fathers Princess Mandane (mother of Cyrus the Great!).

nodes.name: Mandane (Median Princess)
nodes.role: Daughter of Astyages / Mother of Cyrus the Great
nodes.notes: Unites the Median (Madai) and Persian/Elamite (Anshan) royal houses!

nodes.name: Achaemenes (Hakhamanish) → Teispes
nodes.role: Founders of Achaemenid Dynasty (Anshan in Elam)
nodes.notes: Achaemenes -> Teispes (Chishpish), who divides his kingdom between Cyrus I (Anshan/Elam) and Ariaramnes (Persia).

nodes.name: Cyrus I → Cambyses I (Kings of Anshan)
nodes.role: Kings of Anshan (Elam) / Father of Cyrus the Great
nodes.notes: Cambyses I marries Median princess Mandane and fathers Cyrus the Great.

nodes.name: Cyrus the Great (Koresh)
nodes.role: Founder of Persian Empire / Liberator of Judah
nodes.notes: Son of Cambyses I (Anshan/Elam) & Mandane (Media/Madai). Conquers Babylon (539 BCE) and decrees the return of Judean exiles to rebuild Jerusalem! Father of Cambyses II, Bardiya, and Atossa.

nodes.name: Cambyses II, Bardiya & Queen Atossa
nodes.notes: Cambyses II conquers Egypt (525 BCE); Queen Atossa marries Darius I and becomes mother of Xerxes I (Ahasuerus)!

nodes.name: Ariaramnes → Arsames → Hystaspes (Vishtaspa)
nodes.notes: Line from Teispes to Hystaspes, father of Darius I.

nodes.name: Darius I the Great (Darayavahush)
nodes.notes: Son of Hystaspes; marries Cyrus's daughter Atossa, uniting both Achaemenid lines, and confirms Cyrus's decree to complete the Second Temple in Jerusalem.

nodes.name: Xerxes I (Ahasuerus of Book of Esther)
nodes.notes: Son of Darius I & Atossa; widely identified with King Ahasuerus (Achashverosh) in the Book of Esther!

nodes.name: Artaxerxes I → Darius III
nodes.role: Patron of Ezra & Nehemiah → Final Achaemenid
nodes.notes: Son of Xerxes I; commissions Ezra and Nehemiah to rebuild Jerusalem; dynasty continues down to Darius III (Shahnameh's Dara).

nodes.name: Brahma → Svayambhuva Manu & Shatarupa
nodes.notes: Brahma manifests Svayambhuva Manu and Shatarupa as the primordial couple, plus the Seven Sages (Marichi, Atri, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Vashishta).

nodes.name: Marichi → Kashyapa (+ Aditi, Diti, Danu)
nodes.notes: Through Daksha's daughters, Kashyapa fathers the Adityas (including Vivasvan/Surya via Aditi), Daityas, Danavas, Garudas, and Nagas.

nodes.name: Vivasvan (Surya)
nodes.notes: EXACT Proto-Indo-Iranian cognate of Avestan Vivanghant! Father of Yama (Avestan Yima) and Vaivasvata Manu (Great Flood survivor).

nodes.name: Yama & Yami
nodes.role: Twin First Mortals / Exact Cognate of Yima
nodes.notes: Son of Vivasvan; exact linguistic and genealogical twin of Iranian Yima (Jamshid) son of Vivanghant.

nodes.name: Aptya → Trita Aptya & Kavi Ushanas
nodes.role: Exact Proto-Indo-Iranian Cognates of Athwya/Thraetaona & Kavi Usan
nodes.notes: Vedic dragon-slayer Trita son of Aptya is the exact linguistic cognate of Avestan Thraetaona (Fereydun) son of Athwya (Abtin), while sage Kavi Ushanas is the exact cognate of Iranian King Kavi Usan (Kay Kavus)!

nodes.name: Vaivasvata Manu (7th Manu / Flood Survivor)
nodes.role: Vedic Great Flood Survivor (Saved by Matsya)
nodes.notes: Saved by Matsya the Fish during the universal Deluge; ship moored to the Himalayas. Common ancestor of humanity (Manava) in the present age.

nodes.name: Ikshvaku → Raghu → Dasharatha → Rama & Buddha (Shakya)
nodes.notes: Son of Vaivasvata Manu. Produces Harishchandra, Bhagiratha, Raghu, and Prince Rama. Buddhist chronicles (Mahavamsa, Ambattha Sutta) trace Siddhartha Gautama's Shakya clan to King Okkaka = Ikshvaku!

nodes.name: Atri → Soma → Budha + Ila → Pururavas → Yayati
nodes.role: Chandra Vamsha (Lunar Dynasty) / Father of 5 Peoples
nodes.notes: Unites Rishi Atri's lunar line with Vaivasvata Manu's bloodline via Ila. Great-grandson Yayati fathers the five famous Vedic peoples (Panchajana).

nodes.name: Bharata → Kuru → Pandavas & Kauravas (Mahabharata)
nodes.notes: Emperor Bharata gives India its classical name. Descends through Kuru to the Pandavas (Arjuna -> Abhimanyu -> Parikshit).

nodes.name: Yadu (Yadavas → Krishna & Balarama)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Yayati & Devayani; ancestor of the Yadava dynasty including Krishna and Balarama.

nodes.name: Turvasu
nodes.notes: Son of Yayati & Devayani; associated in Puranas with southern/western tribes.

nodes.name: Druhyu (Gandhara / NW Tribes)
nodes.notes: Son of Yayati & Sharmishtha; Puranas trace NW Gandhara and trans-Indus Central Asian/Mleccha tribes to Druhyu!

nodes.name: Anu (Anga, Vanga, Kalinga, Shibi)
nodes.notes: Son of Yayati & Sharmishtha; ancestor of northern and eastern Indian kingdoms.

nodes.name: Puru (Pauravas)
nodes.notes: Youngest son of Yayati & Sharmishtha; inherits the central realm and fathers the Bharata/Kuru dynasty.

nodes.name: Fuxi & Nüwa (Three Sovereigns)
nodes.notes: Serpent-tailed creators who mend heaven after Gonggong's flood and mold humans from yellow clay; preserved in SW Chinese lore as Great Flood survivors.

nodes.name: Yandi (Flame Emperor / Shennong)
nodes.notes: Guoyu records Yandi (Jiang clan) and Huangdi (Ji clan) as half-brothers born of Shaodian; their alliance forms the unified Yan-Huang ancestry.

nodes.name: Huangdi (Yellow Emperor) & Leizu
nodes.role: Universal Royal Ancestor in Sima Qian's Shiji
nodes.notes: Sima Qian traces ALL Five Emperors, all Three Dynasties (Xia, Shang, Zhou), Qin, Chu, and the northern Xiongnu back to Huangdi's 25 sons (14 surnames).

nodes.name: Changyi → Zhuanxu (Gaoyang)
nodes.role: Ancestor of Xia, Shun, Chu & Qin
nodes.notes: Grandson of Huangdi; separates Heaven and Earth; progenitor of Gun -> Yu the Great (Xia), Emperor Shun, and the House of Ying (Qin Shi Huang).

nodes.name: Gun → Yu the Great (Da Yu) → Qi (Xia Dynasty)
nodes.role: Chinese Great Flood Hero & First Hereditary Dynasty
nodes.notes: Dredges rivers to tame the Gun-Yu Great Flood across the Nine Provinces; establishes the Xia Dynasty.

nodes.name: Emperor Ku (Di Ku) → Emperor Yao & Shun
nodes.notes: Great-grandson of Huangdi via Xuanxiao -> Jiaoji; fathers Emperor Yao, Xie (Shang), and Hou Ji (Zhou).

nodes.name: Xie → Tang of Shang (Shang Dynasty → Confucius)
nodes.notes: Historically attested by oracle bones at Anyang; Confucius traced his ancestry to the Shang royal line via the Dukes of Song.

nodes.name: Hou Ji (Lord Millet) → King Wen & Wu (Zhou Dynasty)
nodes.notes: Descended from Di Ku & Jiang Yuan via Hou Ji; established the Mandate of Heaven and classical Chinese philosophy era.

nodes.name: Izanagi & Izanami → Amaterasu & Susanoo
nodes.notes: Create the Japanese archipelago and birth Amaterasu (Sun), Tsukuyomi (Moon), and Susanoo (Storm).

nodes.name: Hwanin → Hwanung + Ungnyeo → Dangun Wanggeom
nodes.notes: Founder of Gojoseon; later annals also link Shang prince Jizi (Gija) migrating to Joseon after 1046 BCE.

nodes.name: Ninigi → Hoori → Emperor Jimmu
nodes.role: Founder of Japan's Continuous Imperial Line
nodes.notes: Descendant of Amaterasu through Ninigi's descent to Mount Takachiho; founder of the Yamato Imperial House.

nodes.name: Chunwei → Xiongnu (Modu Chanyu)
nodes.role: Sima Qian's Bridge Between Chinese Xia & Steppe
